checks_run.procedure:
Review the repair diff 1e0dc5d..dab4562 as code.

Worker configuration (BE-R6, F-DG4-128):
- WORKER_SUPERVISE_INTERVAL_SECONDS: parsing, range and failure mode, in packages/config, main.ts and createBoss/superviseIntervalSecondsOf;
- probe loadConfig directly with edge inputs (config-edge-probe.log).

The preload probe apps/worker/test/interval-probe.mjs must not ship:
- it must be absent from apps/worker/dist after pnpm -r build;
- it must be absent from the runtime tree that deploy/scripts/assemble-runtime.sh (the Dockerfile's own step) builds from a disposable copy.

Also check that no other createBoss caller relies on pg-boss's missing default.
checks_run.command: git diff 1e0dc5d..dab4562 -- packages/config apps/worker .env.example; node --conditions=@mth/source zz-cfgprobe.mjs (temporary, removed); grep -rl interval-probe apps/worker/dist; bash deploy/scripts/assemble-runtime.sh --store-dir $TMPDIR/pstore/v10 $TMPDIR/asm $TMPDIR/asm-out
checks_run.environment: Node 22.22.2. Clone $TMPDIR/probe2 at ea5e262. The runtime assembly ran in a disposable copy, $TMPDIR/asm, deleted afterwards.
checks_run.expected: an integer 1-600 or a refusal naming the variable; exit 78 at start-up; the probe not in the build or the runtime tree
checks_run.actual:
Parsing:
- packages/config/src/load.ts:161 uses the same field() and zod pattern as PORT: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(600).
- Empty or unset gives 60. NAME_FILE is honoured (17 from a file).
- 0, -1, 601, 1.5, NaN, Infinity, 60abc, 9007199254740993 and whitespace-only are refused with 'WORKER_SUPERVISE_INTERVAL_SECONDS is invalid (…)'. The message names the variable, never the value.
- Observation, not a defect: lenient spellings such as '0x3c' (60), '1e1' (10), '6e2' (600), ' 60 ' and '1.0' are accepted. They always resolve to an integer from 1 to 600, exactly as PORT and the rate limits behave.
- Like every catalogue variable, the API also validates it, so an invalid value refuses API start-up too. That is consistent with the existing catalogue.

Failure mode and wiring:
- superviseIntervalSecondsOf (platform.ts:54) throws a RangeError for anything else, so createBoss never passes NaN to pg-boss.
- pg-boss 11.0.0 boss.js:46 is setInterval(…, superviseIntervalSeconds * 1000), which confirms the no-default NaN defect.
- main.ts:22 passes the loaded value. The other createBoss callers are test helpers with supervise:false, or restart tests that pass 1.

The probe does not ship:
- apps/worker/tsconfig.build.json includes only src. 0 files in apps/worker/dist name interval-probe or MTH_INTERVAL_PROBE.
- assemble-runtime exit 0, 'OK 128 packages'. apps/worker in the runtime tree holds only dist, node_modules and package.json, and 0 files name interval-probe, MTH_INTERVAL_PROBE or supervise-cadence. The shipped platform.js does contain superviseIntervalSecondsOf.
- .dockerignore excludes dist, and the image builds from source.

The probe itself only wraps setInterval and reports the delay unchanged.

The script exits correctly (test-script-exit.log, part A PASS):
- rc is 0 only when all three projects pass, and 1 in each of the 7 failing combinations;
- all 3 invocations run every time.
- With an appended '--reporter=verbose', dash ignores the extra argument to 'exit $s'. The rc still follows the projects (0, then 1), but the argument never reaches vitest. Under bash, 'exit: too many arguments' would still give 1. So it fails closed.
- CI runs a bare 'pnpm test' (ci.yml:66), so the dropped argument has no effect on the gate. I record it as an observation, not a defect.
- The real harness run (unit-node22.log) confirms it: unit-web failed, no-codegen still ran, and the script exited 1.

Nothing is weakened:
- setup.ts only imports the page modules (glob src/pages/**, *.test.tsx excluded) in a beforeAll with its own 60 s budget. It does not call lazyPage's load(), so Suspense still runs.
- asyncUtilTimeout stays 5000, and harness-config.test.ts asserts that.
- RouteFallback.test.tsx drives lazyPage with its own controlled promises, so the cache does not affect it. No test mocks a page module.
- session-end.spec.ts only adds a wait for the boot /me (200) and the signed-in shell before the re-login, which makes the 403 csrf case meaningful.

- FE-R10's split root test script exits 1 on any failure in each of the 8 combinations, and always runs all three projects. An argument appended to 'pnpm test' is dropped, which is fail-closed and has no effect on CI (an observation).
- The unit-web warm-up and the session-end wait weaken no test.

- Integration: 1984/1984 with LANG unset and with LANG=C.UTF-8.
- All 15 earlier probes pass unchanged: the sweep 766, IDOR 204, drill scope 163, approvals, Finance, gate commit-time, SoD denials and the scope probes.
